thread:
nina_sales: Heads up - BetaHealth POC hit a blocker. Their F/E calls service.internal.health:443 via their split-horizon DNS. Dig resolves to internal LB IP but TLS cert CN=beta-internal.local. App fails cert validation. Can we advise?

arjun_se: Do we know if they're using an AWS Interface Endpoint or a private NAT path to hosted API? Also asked whether they expect mutual TLS from clients.

nina_sales: They say it's an Interface Endpoint. They also asked if Redwood supports client mTLS for Private deployments.

support-bot: New case created: POC-4018. Please drop any tcpdump/pcap.

sam_eng: Likely split-horizon: their private hosted zone has A record for service.internal pointing at internal ALB that terminates TLS with their cert. Two options: make service.internal resolve to interface endpoint ENI IPs so SNI can be api.redwood.io, or change app to use api.redwood.io as SNI.

kevin_net: Quick checks to ask them to run: 1) dig +short service.internal; 2) curl -v --resolve api.redwood.io:443:<IP> https://api.redwood.io/; 3) openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername service.internal -showcerts

nina_sales: I asked and they returned: dig -> 10.10.50.7, curl without --resolve -> cert CN=beta-internal.local, curl --resolve api.redwood.io:443:10.10.50.7 -> handshake OK with CN=api.redwood.io.

arjun_se: Confirms SNI-based routing. If their app sends SNI=service.internal their handshake will pick the ALB cert. For PrivateLink, AWS private DNS typically maps your public name to the endpoint. Did they enable private DNS on the endpoint?

nina_sales: They said private DNS was disabled because they already have an internal zone for service.internal.

sam_eng: Two customer-friendly routes:
- Quick workaround: update app to use api.redwood.io (or override via hosts) so SNI matches our cert.
- Longer-term: update their private hosted zone record to alias their hostname to the interface endpoint addresses (ENI), or migrate to using AWS Route53 resolver rules so api.redwood.io resolves to the endpoint.

kevin_net: About mTLS: Redwood Private currently does not require client mTLS on the server side for hosted API. For Private deployments we can enable client auth in some enterprise setups but that requires cert enrollment + config on the customer side and a support contract. I'll note this and loop infra.

arjun_se: Add security questionnaire blurb: "Redwood-managed TLS: our service presents server cert for api.redwood.io with OCSP stapling. We rotate certs regularly and maintain CRL/OCSP monitoring. Customer-terminated TLS: if you terminate on your ALB, you must manage cert rotation, OCSP, and CRL. For mutual TLS, Redwood can support client certificate validation on Dedicated/Private deployments under enterprise agreement; contact your SE for provisioning details."

nina_sales: They also asked about billing: if they map service.internal to endpoint ENIs, will traffic be billed differently?

sam_eng: Clarify: traffic that flows over PrivateLink is covered under the Private contract; token usage tracking still applies for api calls. There may be network egress charges on their side for interface endpoints per AWS. I'll ask revenue ops to confirm exact billing language.

kevin_net: Net note: ensure their SGs allow the app subnets to reach the endpoint ENIs on 443. Also confirm no proxy intercepting TLS (e.g., corporate TLS inspection). If they have TLS inspection in the path, you will see internal CA in chain.

nina_sales: They ran tcpdump and attached a short pcap showing TLS ClientHello with SNI=service.internal. I'll ask them to run `tcpdump -nni any port 443 -w /tmp/sni.pcap` and upload.

support-bot: Case POC-4018 updated with pcap.

arjun_se: Next steps I sent to customer: 1) For immediate unblock, change app host header/SNI to api.redwood.io and/or add hosts entry mapping api.redwood.io -> <ENI IP>. 2) For production, update private hosted zone to point service.internal records at the interface endpoint ENI IPs or enable Private DNS on endpoint and remove conflicting records. 3) If you require mTLS, request enterprise enablement and we'll schedule cert exchange.

nina_sales: Customer chose the immediate unblock route and confirmed TLS validated after switching SNI. They want the security blurb for their audit.

arjun_se: Dropping blurb here: "Redwood Private (Interface Endpoint) TLS guidance: - Server identity: Redwood presents a publicly-trusted certificate for api.redwood.io. Clients must present SNI matching api.redwood.io to validate the certificate. - DNS: Prefer enabling AWS Private DNS for the endpoint so api.redwood.io resolves to endpoint ENIs. If you use an internal hostname, point that hostname A record to the endpoint ENI IPs (do not point to your ALB unless you intend to terminate TLS). - OCSP/cert rotation: Redwood rotates server certs and staples OCSP where supported. Customers terminating TLS are responsible for revocation/rotation. - mTLS: Supported for Dedicated/Private on request under an enterprise agreement; requires certificate provisioning and SE coordination."

kevin_net: I'll follow up with infra on mTLS feasibility and timing.

nina_sales: Shared to BetaHealth, they accepted the guidance and we'll close the ticket once infra confirms mTLS options. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
